title: BRAT AI
summary: Conversational family therapy training and assessment application. Parents rehearse difficult conversations with a simulated teen in English or Spanish while a separate real-time evaluator assesses their technique.
myRole: As Product and AI Engineering Lead, I lead Next.js/Node.js development and Azure deployment, and I translate parent-training requirements into the role-play, evaluation, safety and versioning design.

caseStudy.problem: Rehearsing a hard conversation only helps if the simulated teen stays believable, the feedback addresses the right techniques, and sensitive moments are handled safely, in English or Spanish. Asking one model call to role-play and grade at the same time makes both jobs harder to control and to test, and model updates can quietly change how a scenario behaves.

decisions.title: Separate role-play from evaluation
decisions.detail: The simulated teen and the evaluator are separate model roles. The evaluator assesses parenting technique in real time while the role-play continues, so each can be tuned and tested on its own.

decisions.title: Plan for model failures
decisions.detail: Role-play runs on a primary model with fallbacks for errors and context overflow, and speech-to-text falls back through an ordered list of transcription models, so one failed call does not end a practice session.

decisions.title: Pin prompts to each session
decisions.detail: Prompt packs are versioned, and each session keeps the version it started with. An update reaches new sessions without changing one already in progress, which keeps evaluation results comparable across releases.

decisions.title: Layer the guardrails
decisions.detail: Keyword rules and an LLM classifier work together to detect sensitive conversation content and trigger a safety response in under 200 ms. A suite of 95 regression cases covers those paths.

evidence.claim: Dialogue consistency reached 92% on a human-verified golden set covering 5 scenarios at 3 difficulty levels.
Sensitive-content detection reached 95% accuracy on a human-verified golden set, with trigger responses under 200 ms.

tradeoffs: Realism pulls against instructional consistency: a believable teen can drift away from the scenario's learning goal. Measuring dialogue consistency on fixed scenarios keeps that drift visible.
More sensitive guardrails catch more risk but interrupt more legitimate practice. Keyword rules give fast, predictable triggers, and the classifier covers what keywords miss.
Fallback models keep sessions running but can behave differently, which is why prompt versions are pinned and regression cases cover the safety paths.
The golden sets cover defined scenarios and difficulty levels, not every conversation a parent might bring.

publication.title: AI-Caramba: The Experience of Mothers in Central Texas With BRAT, a Parenting AI Chatbot

outcomes: Delivered an English–Spanish role-play and assessment application deployed on Azure.
Paired conversational practice with a separate real-time evaluator and golden-set checks for dialogue consistency and sensitive-content detection.
Maintained 95 regression cases across the safety paths.
